h1:
Lampang Itinerary: 3 Days 2 Nights
Old Town, Chae Son & Elephants
intro: Lampang is an easygoing town you can take slow. The good stuff is spread across the city and the countryside, all within about an hour and a half by car. This 3-day, 2-night plan splits into an old town day with horse carriages and Kad Kong Ta market, a nature day soaking in the hot springs at Chae Son, and a final day seeing elephants at the Thai Elephant Conservation Center before you head home. We've added opening hours, rough prices, and the places locals actually eat at, so you can tweak it however you like.

blocks.html: Lampang sits about 100 km from Chiang Mai, and you can come by train or by car. But if you want to get around without relying on public transport, renting a car or hiring one with a driver is by far the smoothest option, since the highlights like Chae Son and the elephant center are on the opposite side of town from each other. This plan keeps you in the city for both nights and loops you out on day trips, so you don't have to keep changing hotels.

items: Day 1 — Lampang old town, city temples, a horse-carriage ride, and Kad Kong Ta in the evening (Sat–Sun)
Day 2 — Chae Son National Park: soak in the hot springs, splash at the waterfall, boil eggs in the spring
Day 3 — Wat Phra That Lampang Luang, then the Thai Elephant Conservation Center before heading home
Overall budget per person (excluding luxury stays) is roughly THB 2,500–4,000 for 3 days, depending on transport and activities

blocks.title: Line up your day with Kad Kong Ta
blocks.html: Kad Kong Ta market only runs on Saturday and Sunday evenings, around 4 pm to 10 pm. If you want to walk it, plan day one to fall on a weekend. The elephant shows at the conservation center only run at 11 am and 1.30 pm, so save that for late morning on your last day.

blocks.text: Day 1 — Old town, horse carriages and Kad Kong Ta

blocks.html: Spend the first day covering everything in town. Lampang is the only place in Thailand that still has working horse carriages on the streets, and the old town along the Wang River is a pleasant stroll, no long drives needed.

items.activity: Start the morning with rice porridge and coffee at an old shop near the municipal market
items.note: Breakfast the Lampang way — the old town has several spots to choose from. Budget THB 40–70

items.activity: Pay respects at Wat Phra Kaeo Don Tao Suchadaram, a riverside temple by the Wang
items.note: This was once home to the Emerald Buddha. The mix of Lanna and Burmese architecture is gorgeous, and entry is free

items.activity: Take a short horse-carriage loop through the old town, past Ratsadaphisek Bridge and the old wooden houses
items.note: Lampang's carriages have several waiting stands. A city loop starts around THB 200–300 per ride — agree on the price before you get on

items.activity: Northern Thai lunch — khao soi, nam ngiao, or Lampang's famous khuay hoi kha noodles
items.note: Khuay hoi kha noodles are a local specialty, with chewy noodles in a well-rounded broth. Budget THB 50–80

items.activity: Wander Baan Sao Nak, an old teak house built on 116 posts, and learn how Lampang's wealthy families once lived
items.note: Entry is around THB 50, with pretty photo corners and local sweets served

items.activity: Take a café break in the old town and photograph the Sino-Portuguese buildings
items.note: The old Chinese-market district has several cafés set in heritage buildings — a good place to rest before the night market

items.activity: Walk Kad Kong Ta, the riverside walking street along the Wang (Sat–Sun)
items.note: Open 4 pm to 10 pm, with local snacks, craft stalls and old buildings to photograph. On a weekday, swap in another walking street or a riverside restaurant instead

blocks.text: Day 2 — Chae Son National Park hot springs

blocks.html: Today you drive out of town toward Mueang Pan district, about 70 km away and roughly an hour and a half by car. Chae Son is a park with both a waterfall and a hot spring in one place, perfect for a relaxed day with nature.

items.activity: Leave town, stopping to grab sticky rice and snacks for the road
items.note: There are small markets along the way. Bring water and snacks, since food options inside the park are limited

items.activity: Arrive at Chae Son National Park and walk up the 6-tier Chae Son Waterfall
items.note: Open 7 am to 6 pm, adult entry around THB 40. The path up isn't too steep, and kids can manage it

items.activity: Boil eggs at the hot spring, where the water peaks at around 75°C
items.note: The water is hot enough to cook an egg in 15 minutes. Buy a basket of eggs at the spring and boil them yourself — it's fun and the signature thing to do here

items.activity: Lunch at the park restaurant or a made-to-order shop near the entrance
items.note: Local dishes and standard made-to-order fare, at typical national-park prices

items.activity: Soak in the natural mineral pools or a private mineral-bath room
items.note: There's a free foot-soaking pool and paid private mineral-bath rooms — great for easing tired legs after the waterfall

items.activity: Head back into Lampang town
items.note: You'll reach the city by early evening. Save your energy for dinner in town — if you're still up for it, stop for moo kratha or a riverside restaurant on the Wang

blocks.title: Want to stay closer to nature
blocks.html: Chae Son has park bungalows and a campground you can book ahead. If you'd like to wake up to mist and cool air, swap your second night to staying in the park instead of town, then circle back for the elephant center on your last day.

blocks.text: Day 3 — Wat Phra That Lampang Luang and the elephants

blocks.html: Your last day heads west of the city, fitting in the temple Lampang locals are proudest of and time with the elephants before you leave. The two spots are in different districts, but the route between them connects easily.

items.activity: Pack up, check out, and have a light breakfast in town
items.note: Leave time to drive to Wat Phra That Lampang Luang in Ko Kha district, about 18 km away

items.activity: Visit Wat Phra That Lampang Luang, one of the most complete Lanna wooden temples there is
items.note: Open 7.30 am to 5 pm, free entry. The highlights are the upside-down reflection of the chedi inside the dark vihara and the ancient Khong gateway arch

items.activity: Drive on to the Thai Elephant Conservation Center in Hang Chat district
items.note: It's on the Lampang–Chiang Mai road at km 28, open 8.30 am to 3.30 pm, adult entry THB 100

items.activity: Watch the morning elephant 'classroom' show
items.note: Shows are at 11 am and 1.30 pm, with elephant bathing at 10.45 am and 1.15 pm. Arrive a little early for a good seat

items.activity: Feed the elephants and walk through the elephant hospital and feeding grounds
items.note: You can buy sugarcane and bananas to feed them, and there are mahout-life activities for anyone interested

items.activity: Lunch around Hang Chat or somewhere along the way back
items.note: If you're heading to Chiang Mai, this road lines up perfectly. If you're going back to Bangkok, loop back into Lampang town to catch a train or flight

items.activity: Buy souvenirs before you go — rooster bowls, khao taen rice crackers, and northern treats
items.note: The rooster bowl is a Lampang signature, and many ceramic factories have shopfronts where you can buy them

blocks.text: How to pick a place to stay

items.name: Stay in the old town near Kad Kong Ta
items.blurb: Walking distance to the night market and the heritage-building cafés. Great atmosphere and ideal if you don't have a car, with options from budget guesthouses to riverside boutiques

items.name: Stay along the Chiang Mai road
items.blurb: Handy if you're focused on driving out to Chae Son and the elephant center — easy to leave town and plenty of parking

blocks.text: Tips to make the trip smoother

items: Best season to visit — November to February, when it's cool, Chae Son looks its best, and the waterfall still has water
Getting around — public transport in Lampang isn't frequent. For Chae Son and the elephant center, renting a car or hiring one with a driver saves the most time
Cash — markets, local shops, and several park entrances prefer cash, so carry small bills
Opening hours — Kad Kong Ta is Sat–Sun only, and the elephant shows have limited times, so check before you lock in your dates

faq.q: Do you need a car for a 3-day, 2-night Lampang trip?
faq.a: In town you can walk or take a horse carriage just fine. But for Chae Son National Park and the Thai Elephant Conservation Center, which are on opposite sides and far from the city, it's best to rent a car or hire one with a driver, since public transport to these spots is limited and not flexible on timing.

faq.q: How long does it take to get to Chae Son from Lampang town?
faq.a: Chae Son National Park is in Mueang Pan district, about 70 km from the city, roughly an hour and a half by car. Leave early so you have time to walk the waterfall, boil eggs at the hot spring, and soak in the mineral pools all in one day.

faq.q: What times are the elephant shows at the Thai Elephant Conservation Center?
faq.a: The elephant 'classroom' show runs twice, at 11 am and 1.30 pm, with elephant bathing at 10.45 am and 1.15 pm. The center is open 8.30 am to 3.30 pm, with adult entry around THB 100. Come a little before the show for a good seat.

faq.q: When is the best time to visit Lampang?
faq.a: November to February is cool and comfortable, good for both the old town and Chae Son, when the waterfall still has water and the hot spring is at its best. In the rainy season the waterfall runs harder but the paths can get slippery.

faq.q: How much does a 3-day, 2-night Lampang trip cost?
faq.a: Excluding luxury stays, budget roughly THB 2,500–4,000 per person for 3 days, covering food, entrance fees, the horse carriage, and transport to Chae Son and the elephant center. It scales up or down with your choice of accommodation and how you get around.
